c74object.name: mqtt.midi
c74object.description: Sends and receives MIDI with the mqtt-midi topic format, as raw MIDI bytes and through a virtual MIDI port.

discussion.p: mqtt-midi (by Grantler Instruments) puts the message type and channel in the topic and the data in compact binary payloads: {prefix}/{in|out}/cc/{channel}/{controller}, .../noteon/{channel}/{note}, .../noteoff/..., .../program/{channel}, .../pitchbend/{channel}, .../{clock|start|continue|stop} and .../sysex (JSON). Channels are 1-16.
The two sides of mqtt-midi: an instrument listens to in and publishes out; a controller, like the phone app, publishes in and listens to out. direction sets the topics this object listens to.

The inlet and the left outlet carry raw MIDI bytes, like midiout and midiin: use midiformat and midiparse. With port, received messages also play on a virtual MIDI port that Max patches and other applications can open, and what they send to it is published. Virtual ports are available on macOS.
MIDI is published at QoS 0 and never retained. Messages mqtt-midi has no topic for, such as aftertouch, are not sent.

objarg.name: client
objarg.digest: Name of the mqtt.client to use

method.name: int
method.description: Raw MIDI bytes, as midiout takes them, including running status, real-time bytes and SysEx. Complete messages are published.

method.name: list
method.description: A list of raw MIDI bytes.

attribute.name: prefix
attribute.description: The mqtt-midi prefix. Both sides must use the same one.

attribute.name: direction
attribute.description: in: listen to {prefix}/in, publish to {prefix}/out (the instrument side). out: listen to {prefix}/out, publish to {prefix}/in (the controller side).

attribute.name: port
attribute.description: Name of a virtual MIDI port to create. Empty for none.

entry.name: left outlet
entry.description: Received MIDI as raw bytes, one int at a time, as midiin outputs them.

entry.name: middle outlet
entry.description: port with the port name, once Max lists the virtual port as an input and an output device. Connect it to ctlin, notein, ctlout and other MIDI objects: they look up their port when they are created, which in the same patch is before the port exists.
